title: The Shape of an Academic Argument

sections.content: In B2 Unit 35 you met the shape of a short essay. You also know the contrast marker *ahora bien* from B2 Unit 30, *no obstante* from B1 Unit 1, and *si bien* from B2 Unit 8. At C1 these tools become a fixed route that every academic reader expects. The thesis comes first and says what you will defend. A concession grants the best objection. A rebuttal limits it. Evidence backs the thesis, and the conclusion comes back to it in new words. The route works because the reader always knows which move they are reading, so you can write long sentences without getting lost.

sections.title: The moves of one argument
rows: Sostengo que trabajar desde casa mejora la concentración.
I maintain that working from home improves concentration. (thesis)
Es cierto que se pierde parte del contacto con el equipo.
It is true that some contact with the team is lost. (concession)
Ahora bien, ese contacto se puede mantener con reuniones breves.
That said, that contact can be kept up with short meetings. (rebuttal)
Los datos de la empresa respaldan esta idea.
The company's data back up this idea. (evidence)
En definitiva, trabajar desde casa mejora la concentración.
In short, working from home improves concentration. (conclusion)

items.spanish: Mi tesis es que trabajar desde casa mejora los resultados.
items.english: My thesis is that working from home improves results.

items.spanish: Si bien es cierto que el plan es caro, su ventaja es mayor.
items.english: Although it is true that the plan is expensive, its advantage is greater.

items.spanish: Quien no esté de acuerdo debe respaldar su postura con datos.
items.english: Anyone who does not agree must back up their position with data.

items.spanish: El autor fundamenta su tesis en tres ejemplos.
items.english: The author bases his thesis on three examples.

sections.content: English speakers often build up to the claim and put it last. Spanish academic prose states the thesis early and then defends it. Watch the word *argue* too: *discutir* usually means to quarrel or to debate a topic. To say that you maintain a claim, use *sostener que* followed by the indicative: *Sostengo que es viable*. A concession with *si bien* also takes the indicative.
